region: AlUla, Hail, the Harrat volcanic fields and the Najd
title: Saudi Arabia — Nabataean Tombs, Rock Art and Black Lava Fields
subtitle: AlUla, Jubbah and the Harrat: ancient Arabia on a concept that cannot currently be recommended
summary: A concept linking the Nabataean tombs of Hegra, Dadanite inscriptions, UNESCO rock art at Hail and Arabia's volcanic fields. Classified excluded on 27 Nov 2026 because of nationwide official advice and Houthi attacks on airports.
introduction: Northwest Arabia holds some of the least-visited ancient landscapes in the region. At Hegra, more than 100 Nabataean tombs are cut into isolated sandstone outcrops; nearby Dadan and Jabal Ikmah preserve Dadanite and Lihyanite inscriptions in canyon walls. Further east, the Jubbah and Shuwaymis petroglyphs near Hail show ibex, camels and hunters carved over thousands of years, while the black basalt fields of the Harrat stretch towards Khaybar. The Najd plateau adds the Tuwaiq escarpment and the mud-brick quarter of Diriyah. In the current security climate, none of this can be planned: the route is informational only.

exceptional.vsOman: Oman is a coast-to-mountain road trip with wadis and forts; this concept would centre on inland sandstone, Nabataean archaeology and Arabian rock art, with far more controlled site access (guided tours, official transport) and far higher local prices.
exceptional.vsPackageTourism: Standard AlUla packages offer a few hours at Hegra and a sunset experience. This concept adds Hail rock art, volcanic terrain and Najd escarpments that few visitors combine, but it remains informational.
exceptional.vsPortfolio: No other destination in the portfolio combines Nabataean tombs, Dadanite inscriptions, UNESCO rock art and Arabian lava fields; Jordan (D07) shares the Nabataean theme only.

recommendedTravelWindow.rationale: Mid to late March falls after Ramadan and Eid al-Fitr (about 9–10 March), when site hours and restaurants normalise, with warm days and mild nights. Not recommended while the security status stands.

februarySuitability.summary: Best temperatures for walking, but Ramadan starts about 8 February: daytime public eating is prohibited, many restaurants close by day and site hours shift. Security status overrides.

marchSuitability.summary: First part of March is still Ramadan; after about 10 March conditions normalise, though dust and heat build. Security status overrides.

geography.summary: Sandstone rock towers and canyons around AlUla, basalt lava fields (harrat) in the west and the Tuwaiq limestone escarpment of the Najd.
geography.distinctive: The Harrat Khaybar lava field and the AlUla sandstone outcrops sit within a few hours of each other, an unusual pairing of black basalt and orange sandstone.

security.summary: Excluded on 27 Nov 2026. The FCDO advises against all but essential travel to all of Saudi Arabia (and all travel within 10 km of the Yemen border); the Netherlands rates most of the country orange; France formally advises against the south and against Riyadh and Dammam airports. Houthi missile and drone strikes have hit Riyadh airport (10 Oct 2026, 12 reported killed).
security.assessedRoute: Riyadh (arrival), Diriyah, Edge of the World, AlUla, Hail, Harrat Khaybar; Najran and Asir not part of the route.
